public.title: First Bad Version
public.description: badFlags is an array of 0 to 1000 booleans, ordered with all false values before all true values. Entry i describes whether version i+1 fails. Treat reading badFlags[index] as the predicate for that version. Return the 1-based index of the first true value, or -1 when no version fails. Use binary search; functional tests check the boundary, not the number of predicate reads.
hints: Maintain a half-open interval around the first true position.
If the boundary equals the array length, no version fails.
public.attribution: Original statement, examples, tests and solutions authored for Bekor, 2026, for a standard algorithmic problem. No third-party exercise text or solution code used.

explanation: Binary search maintains the boundary between passing and failing versions. The exclusive upper bound permits the no-failure result. O(log n) predicate reads and O(1) space.
